questions.q: You are approaching an intersection, and the green traffic light starts flashing. What does this signal mean?
options: Movement is prohibited; you must stop immediately
Movement is permitted, but a prohibiting signal will come on soon
The traffic light is faulty; the intersection is now uncontrolled
Only a right turn is permitted
questions.explain: Flashing green still permits movement and tells you that its time is running out. It is a prompt to decide in advance whether you can get through or should slow down smoothly.

questions.q: Before a dangerous bend, a traffic light with a single amber signal hangs over the road, and it is flashing. There is no intersection or pedestrian crossing nearby. What should you do?
options: Stop: the amber signal prohibits movement
Stop and wait for the signal to change
Drive carefully: the signal warns of danger
Drive on, giving way to everyone approaching from the right
questions.explain: A flashing amber signal does not prohibit movement: it indicates an uncontrolled intersection or crossing and warns of danger ⟦50⟧. Here there is a dangerous bend ahead, so slow down and be especially careful.

questions.q: At the intersection there is neither a stop line nor sign 5.33 “Stop line”. The light is red for you. Where must you stop?
options: Before the intersecting carriageway, without impeding pedestrians
Right under the traffic light, even if it is at the exit of the intersection
In the middle of the intersection, so as to get through faster later
Anywhere, as long as it is no closer than 10 m to the traffic light
questions.explain: If there is no stop line at an intersection, the driver stops before the intersecting carriageway without impeding pedestrians. Stopping before the traffic light itself applies to other places, not to intersections.

questions.q: The main traffic light signal is amber, and a green filter arrow pointing right is lit in the additional section. You want to turn right. What should you do?
options: Stop: amber prohibits movement in all directions
Turn without slowing down: the arrow gives you priority
Wait for the main signal to turn red, then turn
Turn, giving way to vehicles from other directions
questions.explain: A green filter arrow in the additional section permits a right turn even when the main signal is amber. But when moving in the direction of the arrow while the main signal is amber or red, the driver gives way to vehicles from other directions.

questions.q: The main traffic light signal is a round green, and the additional section with the left arrow is switched off. You want to turn left. May you do so?
options: Yes, the round green main signal permits all directions
No, you may not turn left until the arrow is lit
Yes, but only after giving way to oncoming vehicles
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
questions.explain: An unlit signal in the additional section means that movement is prohibited in the direction it controls. Wait until the arrow comes on.

questions.q: A green arrow pointing left is lit for you. There are no signs prohibiting a U-turn. What are you permitted to do?
options: Only a left turn; a U-turn is prohibited
Only a U-turn; a left turn is prohibited
A left turn or a U-turn
Going straight ahead and left
questions.explain: An arrow permitting a left turn also permits a U-turn, unless a sign prohibits it. Such an arrow does not permit you to go straight ahead.

questions.q: A lane-control signal hangs above your lane, showing a red signal in the shape of the letter “X”. What does this mean?
options: Driving in this lane is prohibited
The lane is for route vehicles only
You must slow down: there are road works ahead
You may use this lane only for overtaking
questions.explain: A lane-control signal showing a red “X” prohibits movement in the lane it is placed above. A green arrow pointing down, on the other hand, permits it.

questions.q: A lane is marked on both sides with marking 1.9. The lane-control signal above it is switched off. May you enter this lane?
options: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic in it
Yes, but only for overtaking
Yes, if you drive no faster than 40 km/h
No, entry to this lane is prohibited
questions.explain: If the lane-control signal above a lane marked on both sides with marking 1.9 is switched off, entry to that lane is prohibited. The direction of traffic in it may have changed.

questions.q: The traffic controller is standing with their left side towards you, arms extended to the sides. You are driving a passenger car. Where may you go?
options: Straight ahead only
In all directions
Straight ahead and right
Movement is prohibited
questions.explain: When the arms are extended to the sides or lowered, trackless vehicles approaching from the left and right sides may go straight ahead and right. A tram in this case may only go straight ahead.

questions.q: The traffic controller is standing with their right side towards you, arms lowered. You are driving a passenger car. Where are you permitted to go?
options: Straight ahead and right
Only to the right
In all directions
Movement is prohibited
questions.explain: Lowered arms mean the same as arms extended to the sides. From the left and right sides, trackless vehicles may go straight ahead and right, while from the chest and back movement is prohibited.

questions.q: The traffic controller is standing with their left side towards you, right arm extended forward. You are in a passenger car and want to turn left. May you do so?
options: No, from the left side only straight ahead and right are permitted
Yes, from the left side all directions are permitted
No, with this signal only a right turn is permitted
No, from this side movement is prohibited for everyone
questions.explain: If the right arm is extended forward, trackless vehicles approaching from the left side may go in all directions, and a tram may turn left.

questions.q: You are crossing a wide street on foot at a controlled intersection. When you are in the middle of the carriageway, the traffic controller raises an arm. You no longer have time to reach the pavement. What should you do?
options: Keep walking: the vehicles will wait until you get across
Stop on the line dividing the opposing traffic flows
Stop right in the lane where the signal caught you
Run diagonally to the nearest corner of the intersection
questions.explain: Pedestrians caught on the carriageway by the traffic controller's raised arm or by an amber signal must clear it. If that is impossible, they stop on the line dividing the traffic flows in opposite directions.

questions.q: The traffic light is green for you, but the traffic controller at the intersection is facing you with arms lowered. What should you do?
options: Go: the green traffic light takes precedence
Go, but straight ahead only
Stop: the controller's signals override traffic lights
Drive on after warning the controller with the horn
questions.explain: From the chest, with the arms lowered, movement is prohibited. A traffic controller's signals must be obeyed even if they contradict traffic lights, road signs or road markings.

questions.q: You are driving at 60 km/h a few metres from the stop line. The green signal went out without flashing, and amber came on immediately. You can stop only by emergency braking. What should you do?
options: Continue through the intersection
Use emergency braking, even with vehicles close behind
Stop on the pedestrian crossing beyond the stop line
Stop and reverse back to the stop line
questions.explain: If the traffic light does not show a flashing green before the green goes out, and a driver cannot stop without emergency braking when amber comes on, the driver continues moving. This is how the Rules protect you from being hit from behind.

questions.q: You are approaching an intersection, and the stop line is still a long way off. The green signal for you has started flashing. What is the right thing to do?
options: Speed up sharply to get through in time
Stop at once, right where the signal caught you
Slow down and get ready to stop at the stop line
Carry on as before: flashing green gives you priority over all
questions.explain: Flashing green still permits movement, but it tells you that its time is running out and a prohibiting signal will come on soon. You are still far away, so it makes sense to slow down in advance and stop calmly at the stop line rather than speed up.

questions.q: The green signal went out without flashing, and amber came on. You are 40 m from the stop line and can stop calmly with normal braking. What must you do?
options: Go through: amber lets you complete the manoeuvre
Stop before the stop line
Go through if there are no pedestrians ahead
Go through with the hazard warning lights on
questions.explain: The amber signal prohibits movement and warns that the signals are about to change. The exception in para. 37 applies only to those who cannot stop without emergency braking. You can stop calmly, so you are obliged to do so.

questions.q: You are first in line at the stop line. The red and amber signals have come on together. May you move off?
options: No: this combination prohibits movement
Yes: this is the signal to move off
Yes, but only to turn right
Yes, if there are no other vehicles at the intersection
questions.explain: The combination of red and amber prohibits movement and only tells you that green will come on soon. You may move off only after the green signal comes on.

questions.q: What does a flashing red traffic light signal mean?
options: The traffic light is faulty; follow the signs
Movement is permitted with extra caution
Movement is prohibited
Only a right turn is permitted
questions.explain: A red signal, including a flashing one, prohibits movement. Flashing red signals are most often installed before level crossings.

questions.q: A green arrow pointing left is lit for you. Sign 3.19 “No U-turn” is placed before the intersection. What are you permitted to do?
options: A left turn and a U-turn
Only a left turn
A left turn and going straight ahead
Nothing: you must wait for the round green signal
questions.explain: An arrow applies only to the direction it shows. A left arrow also permits a U-turn, but only if no sign prohibits it. Here there is sign 3.19, so you may only turn left.

questions.q: You are in the left lane and want to go straight ahead. The main signal is red, and a green filter arrow pointing right is lit in the additional section. May you go?
options: Yes: the additional section opens all directions
No: the red signal prohibits going straight ahead
Yes, if there are no vehicles from other directions
Yes, if you give way to pedestrians first
questions.explain: A green filter arrow permits movement only in its own direction, that is, to the right. For going straight ahead, the red main signal applies, and it prohibits movement.
